checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-TX-TO-PRECOMPILE: secp256r1 point-at-infinity rejection

reachability.notes: Point-at-infinity attacks are a known ECDSA vulnerability.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct a transaction calling the secp256r1 precompile (0x100) with public key (qx=0, qy=0) — the point at infinity. 2. Submit via on-chain transaction. 3. Verify precompile returns empty output (0-length returndata). 4. Test with (0,0) in both compressed and uncompressed forms. 5. Cross-check behavior across all client implementations (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon, Reth) to confirm deterministic rejection.
executable_checks: Deploy contract calling 0x100 with (r, s, qx=0, qy=0) and assert returndata length == 0
Fuzz qx/qy with values (0,0), (p,0), (0,p) and verify consistent rejection
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-EIP7951-PRECOND-005. Boundary edge: EDGE-TX-TO-PRECOMPILE. The identity element must never be accepted as a valid public key.

checklist.title: Verify internal infinity check correctly gates precompile execution

reachability.notes: Point-at-infinity attacks are a known ECDSA vulnerability.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify that the infinity check occurs BEFORE signature verification. 2. Check that both coordinate-level (qx==0 && qy==0) and curve-level infinity representation are handled. 3. Test edge cases: very large coordinates that reduce to identity after modular arithmetic.
executable_checks: Unit test: call check-not-infinity with (0,0) and assert early rejection path taken
Unit test: verify no partial computation occurs when identity is detected
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-EIP7951-PRECOND-005. Node: ACTION-CHECK-NOT-INFINITY. Supporting check ensuring the internal validation correctly feeds the boundary.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-RECEIVE-BLOCK: parent_root validation on P2P blocks

reachability.notes: Attacker sends blocks with unknown parent roots to disrupt fork choice.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Connect a malicious peer to a target node. 2. Send a signed beacon block with a parent_root set to a random 32-byte hash not in the node's store.block_states. 3. Verify the block is REJECTED before any state transition is applied. 4. Confirm no partial state update occurs (e.g., no entry added to block_states). 5. Verify peer scoring penalty is applied.
executable_checks: P2P test: send block with random parent_root, assert rejection
State check: verify store.block_states unchanged after rejection
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-FULUFC-PRECOND-001. Boundary edge: EDGE-RECEIVE-BLOCK (EDGE-P2P-BLOCK-TO-FORKCHOICE). Blocks with unknown parents must be rejected at the boundary.

checklist.title: Verify parent_root lookup in store.block_states is correct and complete

reachability.notes: Attacker sends blocks with unknown parent roots to disrupt fork choice.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify that block_states lookup uses the exact parent_root from the block (not a truncated or modified version). 2. Test with parent_root that was recently pruned (finalized and removed). 3. Verify that blocks referencing the genesis block's root are handled correctly.
executable_checks: Test: block with parent_root of finalized-and-pruned block, assert rejection
Test: block with valid parent_root, assert acceptance
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-FULUFC-PRECOND-001. Node: ACTION-CHECK-PARENT-KNOWN. Supporting check for internal state lookup correctness.

checklist.title: Falsify checkpoint update post-condition after block acceptance

reachability.notes: Incorrect checkpoint updates could stall finality.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Process a block whose post-state has a new justified checkpoint higher than the current store justified checkpoint. 2. Verify update_checkpoints is called with the post-state's current_justified_checkpoint and finalized_checkpoint. 3. Attempt to falsify: process a block and verify that store.justified_checkpoint is NOT updated when it should be (bug: missing call). 4. Check edge case: block whose post-state justified checkpoint equals the store's current one (no-op expected).
executable_checks: State test: after block with new justified checkpoint, assert store.justified_checkpoint updated
State test: after block with same justified checkpoint, assert store.justified_checkpoint unchanged
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-FULUFC-POSTCOND-002. Formal Verification mindset: attempting to find a state transition where checkpoints are not updated when they should be.

checklist.title: Falsify proposer_lookahead vector size invariant across epoch transitions

reachability.notes: Incorrect vector size could cause index-out-of-bounds or wrong proposer assignment.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Process epoch transitions and verify proposer_lookahead has exactly 2 * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH entries after each epoch processing. 2. Attempt to violate: process multiple consecutive epochs and check for vector growth or shrinkage. 3. Test fork initialization: verify the vector contains entries for remaining current epoch + lookahead epochs. 4. Test edge case: epoch transition at fork boundary where lookahead format changes.
executable_checks: Epoch test: after process_epoch, assert len(state.proposer_lookahead) == 2 * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH
Fork init test: after upgrade_to_fulu, assert proposer_lookahead covers correct slot range
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-EIP7917-INV-001. Formal Verification mindset: attempting to find epoch transitions that violate the size invariant.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-VALIDATOR-RANDAO-TO-LOOKAHEAD: EB lock timing

reachability.notes: Using current EB instead of locked EB enables grinding.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. At epoch N, note all validators' effective balances. 2. A malicious validator changes their effective balance between epoch N and N+1 (via deposits/withdrawals). 3. Verify that proposer computation for epoch N + MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1 uses the EB values from epoch N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD - 1, NOT the current epoch. 4. Compare proposer lists with historical vs current EB values to detect grinding vulnerability.
executable_checks: Test: modify validator EB after RANDAO reveal, verify proposer schedule unchanged
Test: verify get_beacon_proposer_index uses historical EB snapshot
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-EIP7917-PRECOND-002. Boundary edge: EDGE-VALIDATOR-RANDAO-TO-LOOKAHEAD. Anti-grinding security depends on EB lock timing.

checklist.title: Verify EB snapshot is correctly taken at epoch N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD - 1

reachability.notes: Using current EB instead of locked EB enables grinding.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify that the EB values used in compute_proposer_index are from the state at epoch N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD - 1. 2. Check for off-by-one errors in the epoch offset calculation. 3. Verify this holds across fork boundaries.
executable_checks: Unit test: trace EB source epoch in compute_proposer_index, assert correct lookback
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-EIP7917-PRECOND-002. Node: STATE-EB-VALUES-LOCKED. Supporting internal check.

checklist.title: Falsify CLZ opcode fork activation boundary behavior

reachability.notes: Fork boundary handling: transactions in the activation block must use the correct behavior.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Deploy a contract using opcode 0x1e in the block immediately BEFORE Fusaka activation. Verify it causes INVALID opcode exception. 2. Execute the same contract in the exact Fusaka activation block. Verify CLZ executes correctly. 3. Test the block BEFORE activation (off-by-one). 4. Cross-check all client implementations for identical activation block behavior.
executable_checks: Test: execute 0x1e opcode at block N-1 (pre-fork), assert INVALID
Test: execute 0x1e opcode at block N (fork block), assert CLZ result correct
Cross-client: compare gas consumption for CLZ across all clients
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-EIP7939-PRECOND-003. Related ambiguity: AMB-EIP7939-02. Pre-condition: fork activation boundary must be exact.

checklist.title: Falsify validation pipeline ordering invariant in fork choice

reachability.notes: If DA check runs before parent check, it could trigger expensive KZG verification for orphan blocks (DoS vector).

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Send a block with an unknown parent_root but valid-looking data column sidecars. 2. Monitor whether the node performs KZG verification BEFORE rejecting for unknown parent. 3. If KZG verification occurs, the pipeline ordering is violated (expensive computation on invalid block). 4. Measure CPU time spent on the invalid block to quantify DoS potential.
executable_checks: P2P test: send orphan block with valid sidecars, measure time before rejection
Code audit: verify on_block checks parent_root before calling is_data_available
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-FULUFC-INV-006. Invariant: validation order must be parent→slot→finalized→ancestry→DA.

checklist.title: Falsify custody group assignment determinism across implementations

reachability.notes: Non-deterministic custody assignment would cause nodes to disagree on data availability obligations, causing network splits.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Call get_custody_groups with identical (node_id, custody_group_count) across all client implementations. 2. Verify outputs are identical sets. 3. Test edge cases: node_id = 0, node_id = 2^256-1, custody_group_count = 1, custody_group_count = NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS. 4. Call the function 1000 times with the same inputs and verify all outputs are identical (detect non-determinism from uninitialized memory or hash randomization).
executable_checks: Cross-client test: same (node_id, count) produces same group set in all clients
Fuzz: random node_ids, verify deterministic output across repeated calls
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-DASCORE-INV-001. Formal Verification mindset: attempting to find inputs causing divergent custody assignments.

checklist.title: Falsify matrix reconstruction completeness and KZG consistency

reachability.notes: Corrupted reconstruction would propagate bad data via re-gossip.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Provide exactly 50% of columns (minimum for recovery) and reconstruct the full matrix. 2. Verify all 128 columns are present after reconstruction. 3. Re-verify KZG proofs on ALL reconstructed columns against original commitments. 4. Attempt to falsify: provide 49% of columns (below threshold) and verify reconstruction fails gracefully. 5. Provide adversarially chosen column subsets to test recovery correctness.
executable_checks: Test: reconstruct from 50% columns, verify all 128 present and KZG-valid
Test: reconstruct from 49% columns, verify graceful failure
Test: reconstruct from adversarial column subset, verify KZG consistency
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-DASCORE-POSTCOND-005. Post-condition: all columns must be recoverable and KZG-consistent.

checklist.title: Falsify fork activation timestamp comparison correctness

reachability.notes: Premature fork activation due to timestamp comparison bug would cause consensus split.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify that fork rules are NOT applied when block.timestamp < activation_timestamp. 2. Verify fork rules ARE applied when block.timestamp == activation_timestamp (boundary). 3. Verify fork rules ARE applied when block.timestamp > activation_timestamp. 4. Test with timestamp = activation_timestamp - 1, activation_timestamp, activation_timestamp + 1. 5. Cross-client comparison of activation logic.
executable_checks: Test: block at timestamp activation-1, assert pre-fork rules
Test: block at timestamp activation, assert post-fork rules
Test: block at timestamp activation+1, assert post-fork rules
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP7607-PRECOND-001. Pre-condition: >= comparison required.

checklist.title: Falsify MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE constant consistency across clients

reachability.notes: Different clients using different MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE values would cause consensus divergence.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE == 8,388,608 (8 MiB = 8 * 1024 * 1024) in each client implementation. 2. Construct a block with RLP size exactly 8,388,608 bytes and verify acceptance. 3. Construct a block with RLP size 8,388,609 bytes and verify rejection. 4. Cross-client: submit boundary-size block and verify identical accept/reject decision.
executable_checks: Cross-client: verify constant value 8388608 in source code
Test: block at exactly 8388608 bytes RLP, assert accepted
Test: block at 8388609 bytes RLP, assert rejected
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP7934-INV-001. Invariant: constant must be exactly 8 MiB.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-PARSE-0x10: RLP nil literal handling in PooledTransactions

reachability.notes: Incorrect handling of RLP nil literals for elided blob payloads could cause type confusion or null pointer dereferences.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct a PooledTransactions (0x10) response containing a type-3 transaction with blob payload fields set to RLP nil literals (0x80). 2. Send via P2P to target node. 3. Verify the node correctly parses nil as 'elided blob payload' (not as empty bytes or as an error). 4. Verify no null pointer dereference or type confusion occurs. 5. Test malformed nil variants (truncated RLP, wrong length prefix).
executable_checks: P2P test: send PooledTransactions with nil blob payload, assert correct parsing
P2P test: send malformed nil literal variants, assert graceful rejection
Cross-client: verify identical behavior for nil literal handling
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP8070-PRECOND-004. Boundary edge: EDGE-PARSE-0x10 (EDGE-PEER-CELLS-RESPONSE). Trust boundary for P2P deserialization.

checklist.title: Falsify noise column indistinguishability in GetCells requests

reachability.notes: If the provider can identify which column is the noise column (e.g., by knowing the requester's custody set via ENR), they can selectively serve only that column while withholding custody columns.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Examine if a provider can determine the requester's custody groups from their ENR (custody_group_count field). 2. If custody groups are known, check if the noise column can be identified by elimination (requested columns minus known custody columns = noise column). 3. If identifiable, verify whether a provider can selectively serve only the noise column while withholding custody columns. 4. Test: as a provider, attempt to identify noise vs custody columns in requests.
executable_checks: Analysis: given requester ENR with cgc, compute custody groups and identify noise column
P2P test: verify noise column selection is not predictable from ENR data alone
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP8070-INV-003. Invariant: noise column must be indistinguishable from custody columns to the provider.

checklist.title: Falsify eth/69 handshake compatibility invariant maintenance throughout connection

reachability.notes: Ensures all connected peers remain compatible

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Complete an eth/69 handshake with a peer. 2. Verify networkid, genesis hash, and forkid are validated during handshake. 3. Attempt to violate: after handshake, simulate a fork update that makes the peer incompatible and verify the connection is dropped. 4. Test: peer sends Status with valid fields but then sends messages inconsistent with claimed fork version.
executable_checks: P2P test: complete handshake, then verify fork compatibility is rechecked at fork transitions
P2P test: peer with mismatched networkid during handshake, assert disconnect
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W2-EIP7642-HANDSHAKE-INV-01. Invariant: compatibility must hold throughout connection lifetime.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-REQUEST-RECEIPTS: GetReceipts request validation

reachability.notes: Untrusted peers can request receipts

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Send a GetReceipts request with an excessive number of block hashes (e.g., 10,000). 2. Verify the node either limits the request size or rate-limits the response. 3. Check that malformed request parameters (invalid hash lengths, empty requests) are handled gracefully.
executable_checks: P2P test: send GetReceipts with 10000 hashes, verify bounded response
P2P test: send malformed GetReceipts, verify graceful handling
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W2-EIP7642-RECEIPT-PRECOND-01. Boundary edge: EDGE-REQUEST-RECEIPTS. Low severity per scope: standard request limiting expected.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for gossip data_column_sidecar: proposer signature verification

reachability.notes: Cryptographic authentication of block proposer

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct a data_column_sidecar with a valid structure but an invalid proposer signature on signed_block_header. 2. Gossip it to target node. 3. Verify REJECT with peer penalty. 4. Test: valid signature but wrong proposer key (not the expected proposer for that slot). 5. Test: signature over different data (replay from different slot).
executable_checks: P2P test: gossip sidecar with random signature, assert REJECT
P2P test: gossip sidecar with valid sig from wrong proposer, assert REJECT
P2P test: replay sidecar from different slot, assert REJECT
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W2-FULU-GOSSIP-PRECOND-05. Boundary edge: EDGE-GOSSIP-DATA-COLUMN-SIDECAR. Rule 5 of gossip validation.

checklist.title: Falsify gossip validation completeness: all 13 rules must pass for acceptance

reachability.notes: Strongest postcondition: acceptance implies all validations passed

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. For each of the 13 validation rules, construct a sidecar that fails ONLY that rule and passes all others. 2. Verify each is REJECTED. 3. This proves no single rule can be bypassed. 4. Pay special attention to rule ordering: if a later rule is checked before an earlier one, a short-circuit could skip intermediate rules. 5. Test race conditions: submit sidecar during epoch transition when validator set is changing.
executable_checks: 13 targeted tests: one sidecar failing each individual rule, all others passing, assert REJECT for each
Positive test: sidecar passing all 13 rules, assert ACCEPT
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W2-FULU-GOSSIP-INV-01. This is the strongest postcondition for PeerDAS gossip security.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-EL-TRUST: engine_getBlobsV2 trust assumption

attacker_controlled: Blob data if EL is compromised
validation_layers: NONE - verification explicitly skipped per AMB-FULU-P2P-05
reachability.notes: CRITICAL: ASSUM-FULU-P2P-01 and AMB-FULU-P2P-05 - EL is trusted, no KZG verification on local blobs

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Simulate a compromised EL that returns corrupted blob data via engine_getBlobsV2. 2. Verify whether the CL converts these corrupted blobs into data columns WITHOUT KZG verification. 3. If yes, verify these corrupted columns are gossiped to the network. 4. Assess impact: how many nodes would accept the corrupted columns before KZG verification catches them at gossip validation on receiving peers. 5. Check: does the anti-equivocation cache cover locally-imported columns?
executable_checks: Integration test: mock EL returning corrupted blobs, verify CL behavior
Verify: CL skips KZG for local blobs (confirm the trust assumption)
Verify: anti-equivocation cache includes locally-imported data columns
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W2-FULU-BLOB-PUB-PRECOND-01. CRITICAL trust boundary. Boundary edge: EDGE-ENGINE-API-GET-BLOBS-V2. Related: AMB-FULU-P2P-04 (SHOULD→MUST upgrade recommended).

checklist.title: Falsify fork transition epoch boundary requirement

reachability.notes: Fork at a non-epoch boundary would corrupt state transition logic.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Attempt to trigger fork upgrade at a slot that is NOT an epoch boundary (slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH != 0). 2. Verify the upgrade is rejected. 3. Trigger upgrade at exact epoch boundary and verify success. 4. Test: slot = SLOTS_PER_EPOCH * N - 1 (one before boundary), slot = SLOTS_PER_EPOCH * N (at boundary), slot = SLOTS_PER_EPOCH * N + 1 (one after).
executable_checks: Test: upgrade_to_fulu at non-epoch-boundary slot, assert rejection
Test: upgrade_to_fulu at epoch boundary, assert success
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-FULU-FORK-TRANSITION-PRE-001. Pre-condition: slot must be at epoch boundary.

checklist.title: Falsify active validator set derivation for proposer computation

reachability.notes: Wrong active validator set would produce incorrect proposer selection.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. At epoch boundary, compute active validator indices using get_active_validator_indices(state, epoch). 2. Verify the set includes only validators with activation_epoch <= epoch < exit_epoch. 3. Attempt to falsify: check if validators pending activation or pending exit are incorrectly included/excluded. 4. Test edge case: validator whose activation_epoch == target_epoch (should be included).
executable_checks: Test: validator with activation_epoch == epoch, assert included in active set
Test: validator with exit_epoch == epoch, assert excluded from active set
Test: verify proposer computation uses correct epoch's active set
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-FULU-BEACON-LOOKAHEAD-PRE-002. Pre-condition for proposer lookahead computation.

checklist.title: Falsify fork digest determinism and blob-parameter sensitivity

reachability.notes: If XOR + truncation produces collisions for different blob params, incompatible nodes could connect.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Compute fork digest with identical (fork_version, genesis_validators_root, blob_params) on two nodes, verify identical result. 2. Change ONE blob parameter (e.g., MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK) and recompute, verify DIFFERENT digest. 3. Test for hash collisions: enumerate plausible blob parameter sets and check for 4-byte digest collisions. 4. Cross-client: verify all clients produce identical digests for the same inputs.
executable_checks: Test: identical inputs produce identical fork digest across clients
Test: different blob params produce different fork digest
Collision test: enumerate parameter space for 4-byte collisions
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-FULU-FORK-DIGEST-INV-001. Related assumption: ASSUM-FULU-BEACON-05.

checklist.title: Falsify blob schedule synchronization across client implementations [CONDITIONAL SCOPE]

reachability.notes: No protocol-level enforcement of blob schedule updates. Relies on client teams shipping correct updates.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify all client implementations have identical BLOB_SCHEDULE configuration for each scheduled epoch. 2. Check default values in each client's config files. 3. Attempt to falsify: configure one client with a different blob schedule and verify it forks from the network. 4. NOTE: This is CONDITIONAL scope — requires further investigation whether protocol-level enforcement exists.
executable_checks: Cross-client: compare BLOB_SCHEDULE constants in all client source code
Test: client with wrong blob schedule, verify it rejects valid post-change blocks
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-FULU-BLOB-SCHEDULE-INV-004. CONDITIONAL SCOPE: no protocol-level enforcement. Related assumption: ASSUM-FULU-BEACON-04.

checklist.title: Falsify reserve price evaluation continuity across blocks

reachability.notes: Skipping the reserve check on some blocks would produce incorrect excess values.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct a sequence of blocks that transitions from normal pricing to reserve pricing mode. 2. Verify excess_blob_gas trajectory is smooth (no discontinuities). 3. Attempt to falsify: find an input sequence where the mode transition creates a jump in excess_blob_gas. 4. Verify the reserve price condition is evaluated on EVERY block (not cached or skipped). 5. Cross-client: verify identical excess_blob_gas values for the same block sequence.
executable_checks: Test: block sequence crossing normal→reserve boundary, verify no excess_blob_gas jump
Test: block sequence crossing reserve→normal boundary, verify smooth transition
Cross-client: identical block sequence produces identical excess_blob_gas in all clients
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-EIP7918-RESERVE-INV-002. Related ambiguity: AMB-EIP7918-01.

checklist.title: Falsify RANDAO mix finalization for proposer seed computation

reachability.notes: Validators can manipulate RANDAO reveals to bias proposer selection. MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD mitigates this but the window is small.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify that process_proposer_lookahead uses RANDAO mixes from a finalized epoch (before current epoch's RANDAO was revealed). 2. Verify the seed used is from epoch N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD - 1. 3. Attempt to falsify: check if a validator withholding their RANDAO reveal at epoch boundary can influence the next epoch's proposer schedule. 4. Test with EIP-7917 deterministic lookahead: verify the lookahead is computed using the correct historical RANDAO mix.
executable_checks: Test: verify get_seed uses RANDAO mix from correct historical epoch
Test: validator skips RANDAO reveal, verify proposer schedule unaffected for target epoch
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-FULU-BEACON-RANDAO-INV-001. RANDAO manipulation is a known risk, but EIP-7917 changes impact by making assignments visible earlier.

checklist.title: Falsify fork digest blob parameter incorporation post-condition

reachability.notes: If blob parameter changes don't affect fork digest, peers on different schedules could connect.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Call compute_fork_digest with blob parameters A. Record digest. 2. Call compute_fork_digest with blob parameters B (differing in one field). Record digest. 3. Verify digests are different. 4. Test: all possible single-field changes in blob parameters produce different digests. 5. Test: identical parameters always produce identical digests.
executable_checks: Test: different MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK produces different fork digest
Test: different TARGET_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK produces different fork digest
Test: identical params produce identical fork digest
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-FULU-BLOB-SCHEDULE-POST-002. Post-condition: blob params must be incorporated into fork digest.

checklist.title: Falsify BPO fork activation timestamp boundary on EL

reachability.notes: Off-by-one in timestamp comparison at fork boundary could cause the first post-fork block to use wrong parameters.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Set bpoTime to a known timestamp T. 2. Submit block with timestamp T-1: verify pre-BPO parameters used. 3. Submit block with timestamp T: verify post-BPO parameters used (>= comparison). 4. Submit block with timestamp T+1: verify post-BPO parameters used. 5. Cross-client: verify all EL implementations use >= (not >) for activation comparison.
executable_checks: Test: block.timestamp == bpoTime - 1, assert pre-fork blob params
Test: block.timestamp == bpoTime, assert post-fork blob params
Cross-client: verify >= comparison in all EL implementations
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W4-EIP7892-PRECOND-003. Pre-condition: >= comparison at exact activation timestamp.

checklist.title: Falsify ModExp gas cost floor of 500 across all input combinations

reachability.notes: Attacker could craft inputs targeting the minimum gas path. If the floor is bypassed, extremely cheap ModExp calls enable DoS.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Call ModExp with minimal inputs: base_length=0, exponent_length=0, modulus_length=0. Verify gas cost >= 500. 2. Call with base_length=1, exponent_length=1, modulus_length=1 with all-zero values. Verify gas cost >= 500. 3. Fuzz: generate random (base_length, exponent_length, modulus_length) tuples, verify gas cost is always >= 500. 4. Cross-client: verify all implementations enforce the 500 floor identically.
executable_checks: Test: ModExp(0,0,0) gas cost >= 500
Test: ModExp(1,1,1) with zero values, gas cost >= 500
Fuzz: 10000 random inputs, assert gas >= 500 for all
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W4-EIP7883-INV-001. Invariant: gas floor of 500 must hold for ALL inputs.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for BOUNDARY-DAS-COLUMN-SAMPLING: KZG proof verification on P2P column samples

reachability.notes: Malicious P2P peer can send column samples with invalid KZG proofs. If verification is skipped or flawed, node may accept invalid data as available.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct column samples with valid structure but invalid KZG proofs (random bytes for proofs). 2. Send via P2P sampling response. 3. Verify node rejects the column and does NOT count it toward DA confirmation. 4. Test: valid column with one bit-flipped proof byte. 5. Test batch verification: verify a single invalid proof in a batch causes the entire batch to fail.
executable_checks: P2P test: column with random KZG proof bytes, assert rejection
P2P test: column with single-bit-flipped proof, assert rejection
Batch test: batch of 10 columns with 1 invalid, assert batch rejection
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7594-DAS-PRECOND-001. Boundary edge: BOUNDARY-DAS-COLUMN-SAMPLING. CRITICAL: this is the foundation of DAS security.

checklist.title: Falsify pseudorandom sampling function determinism across clients

reachability.notes: Non-deterministic or divergent sampling algorithms would cause nodes to sample different columns, breaking statistical security guarantees.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Call the sampling function with identical (node_id, slot) across all client implementations. 2. Verify identical column indices selected. 3. Test edge cases: slot=0, slot=MAX_UINT64, node_id=0, node_id=MAX. 4. Verify the function uses a specified cryptographic hash (not implementation-specific PRNG). 5. Run 10000 iterations with same inputs, verify deterministic output.
executable_checks: Cross-client: identical (node_id, slot) produces identical sample set
Determinism test: 10000 calls with same inputs produce identical output
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7594-DAS-AMB-002. Related ambiguity: AMB-EIP7594-02.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for blob transaction rejection on proof failure

reachability.notes: If failed verification does not properly reject, invalid blob transactions leak into the mempool and propagate.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct a type-3 blob transaction with valid structure but invalid cell KZG proofs. 2. Submit via P2P transaction gossip. 3. Verify the transaction is NOT added to the mempool. 4. Verify it is NOT re-gossiped to other peers. 5. Test: verify the rejection happens synchronously (no race between validation and mempool insertion).
executable_checks: P2P test: submit blob tx with invalid cell proofs, verify not in mempool
P2P test: verify invalid blob tx not re-gossiped

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for BOUNDARY-MODEXP-CALL: exponent length upper bound

reachability.notes: Exponent length is attacker-controlled via on-chain transaction calldata.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Call MODEXP with exponent_length = 1025 (one above limit). Verify rejection with all gas consumed. 2. Call with exponent_length = 1024 (at limit). Verify acceptance. 3. Call with exponent_length = 2^256-1 (maximum uint). Verify rejection before any computation. 4. Verify the length check occurs BEFORE memory allocation and computation. 5. Cross-client: all implementations reject at the same threshold.
executable_checks: Test: MODEXP with exp_length=1025, assert all gas consumed and empty return
Test: MODEXP with exp_length=1024, assert successful execution
Test: MODEXP with exp_length=2^32, assert rejection before computation
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7823-VAL-PRECOND-002. Boundary edge: BOUNDARY-MODEXP-CALL. Input bound: 1024 bytes.

checklist.title: Falsify MODEXP violation gas exhaustion post-condition

reachability.notes: Gas accounting post-violation must leave exactly zero gas in the call frame.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Call MODEXP with an oversized input (violation) from a call frame with known gas amount G. 2. After the precompile returns, verify remaining gas in the call frame is exactly 0. 3. Attempt to falsify: check if any gas remains (would allow post-violation computation to differ between clients). 4. Test: nested calls — outer frame calls MODEXP with violation, verify outer frame sees the inner frame exhausted.
executable_checks: Test: MODEXP violation with G gas, assert 0 remaining after call
Test: nested call with MODEXP violation, verify caller sees correct gas deduction
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7823-GAS-POSTCOND-001. Post-condition: exactly zero gas must remain.

checklist.title: Falsify per-transaction gas cap vs block-level gas distinction

reachability.notes: If a client incorrectly applies the per-tx cap as a block-level cap, it would reject valid blocks.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct a block with multiple transactions where each tx.gasLimit <= 16,777,216 but total block gas used > 16,777,216. 2. Verify the block is ACCEPTED (the cap is per-tx, not per-block). 3. Construct a block with a single tx where tx.gasLimit = 16,777,217. 4. Verify the block is REJECTED. 5. Cross-client: verify all implementations accept the multi-tx block and reject the single over-cap tx.
executable_checks: Test: block with 3 txs each at 10M gas (total 30M), assert accepted
Test: block with 1 tx at 16777217 gas, assert rejected
Cross-client: identical accept/reject for boundary cases
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7825-BLK-AMB-001. Related ambiguity: AMB-EIP7825-03. Key: cap is per-transaction, not per-block.

checklist.title: Falsify premature Fulu fork activation guard

reachability.notes: Premature fork activation would split the network.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Process slots at epoch FULU_FORK_EPOCH - 1. Verify state remains in Electra format. 2. Process a slot at epoch FULU_FORK_EPOCH. Verify fork upgrade triggers. 3. Attempt to falsify: check if any code path can trigger Fulu upgrade before FULU_FORK_EPOCH. 4. Test: check integer overflow scenarios if FULU_FORK_EPOCH is set to MAX_UINT64 (disabled).
executable_checks: Test: epoch = FULU_FORK_EPOCH - 1, assert Electra state format
Test: epoch = FULU_FORK_EPOCH, assert Fulu state format
Test: FULU_FORK_EPOCH = FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH, assert fork never triggers
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W6-FULU-FORK-ST-INV-002. Invariant: no Fulu upgrade outside FULU_FORK_EPOCH.

checklist.title: Falsify proposer_lookahead initialization ordering at fork boundary

reachability.notes: Race condition where block validation occurs before lookahead is initialized could cause undefined behavior.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. At the exact Fulu fork transition, verify proposer_lookahead is fully initialized BEFORE any block proposal or validation occurs. 2. Attempt to falsify: submit a block for validation at the first post-fork slot and verify the lookahead is populated. 3. Test: check if there's a window between fork upgrade and lookahead initialization where block validation could be attempted.
executable_checks: Test: at first post-fork slot, verify state.proposer_lookahead is non-empty
Test: block validation at first post-fork slot succeeds (lookahead available)
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W6-FULU-FORK-CON-PRECOND-001. Related ambiguity: AMB-FULU-FORK-03. Pre-condition: lookahead must be initialized before use.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for sidecar reconstruction: input integrity validation

reachability.notes: A malicious peer could send a crafted sidecar that passes initial checks but causes errors during reconstruction.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct a sidecar with valid headers/signature but corrupted cell data (passes signature check, fails during reconstruction). 2. Send via P2P. 3. Verify the node does not crash during get_data_column_sidecars_from_column_sidecar. 4. Test: sidecar with truncated cell data, extra cells, mismatched column indices. 5. Verify error handling returns a proper error rather than panicking.
executable_checks: P2P test: sidecar with corrupted cell data, assert no crash during reconstruction
P2P test: sidecar with truncated cells, assert graceful rejection
P2P test: sidecar with extra cells, assert rejection
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W6-FULU-VAL-SIDECAR-PRECOND-003. Related ambiguity: AMB-FULU-VALIDATOR-04.

checklist.title: Falsify erasure coding reconstruction threshold invariant

reachability.notes: If erasure coding is weaker than expected, a block producer could withhold data while passing sampling checks.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Attempt reconstruction with exactly (threshold - 1) columns. Verify it FAILS. 2. Attempt reconstruction with exactly threshold columns. Verify it SUCCEEDS and output matches original data. 3. Verify the threshold is CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB / 2. 4. Test: adversarially chosen column subsets at threshold-1 count, verify no successful reconstruction.
executable_checks: Test: reconstruction from threshold-1 columns fails
Test: reconstruction from threshold columns succeeds with correct output
Test: verify threshold == CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB / 2
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W6-FULU-VAL-RETAIN-INV-002. Related assumption: ASSUM-FULU-VALIDATOR-03. CRITICAL: data availability security depends on this.

checklist.title: Falsify history expiry activation sequence enforcement

reachability.notes: Premature mainnet activation before Pectra could break CL deposit processing.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify that history expiry configuration for mainnet requires Pectra fork to be active. 2. Attempt to enable history expiry before Pectra activation epoch. 3. Verify the client refuses or warns. 4. Test: check if there's a configuration flag that could bypass the Pectra prerequisite.
executable_checks: Config test: verify mainnet history expiry config requires PECTRA_ACTIVATION_EPOCH
Test: attempt activation before Pectra, assert rejection or warning
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W6-EIP7927-ACT-INV-001. Related ambiguity: AMB-EIP7927-01. Configuration-dependent but could break deposit processing.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-BLOCK-GOSSIP-CL: block size validation at CL gossip

reachability.notes: An adversarial block builder can construct worst-case blocks via P2P. If block size validation is missing or incorrect, oversized blocks could crash CL nodes or disrupt gossip.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct a valid block that approaches but does not exceed the 10 MiB CL gossip limit. Verify it is accepted. 2. Construct a block that exceeds 10 MiB serialized size. Gossip it to the network. 3. Verify receiving nodes REJECT the oversized block BEFORE deserialization. 4. Verify the 10 MiB limit is checked on the raw serialized bytes, not after decompression. 5. Test: block at exactly 10,485,760 bytes vs 10,485,761 bytes.
executable_checks: P2P test: gossip block at 10 MiB, assert accepted
P2P test: gossip block at 10 MiB + 1 byte, assert rejected
Verify: size check occurs before deserialization
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W7-EIP7935-SECBND-PRECOND-001. Boundary edge: EDGE-BLOCK-GOSSIP-CL. Related assumption: ASSUM-EIP7935-03.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-BLOB-ENGINE-API: blob length validation before polynomial encoding

reachability.notes: Blob data from Engine API (semi-trusted) or network could have incorrect length. Missing validation could cause buffer overflows or incorrect polynomial encoding.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Provide a blob with BYTES_PER_BLOB - 1 bytes. Verify rejection before polynomial conversion. 2. Provide a blob with BYTES_PER_BLOB + 1 bytes. Verify rejection. 3. Provide a blob with exactly BYTES_PER_BLOB bytes. Verify acceptance. 4. Provide an empty blob (0 bytes). Verify rejection. 5. Test via mock Engine API: return malformed blob lengths.
executable_checks: Test: blob with BYTES_PER_BLOB - 1 bytes, assert rejection
Test: blob with BYTES_PER_BLOB + 1 bytes, assert rejection
Test: blob with BYTES_PER_BLOB bytes, assert acceptance
Test: empty blob, assert rejection
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W7-PCS-ENCODE-PRECOND-001. Boundary edge: EDGE-BLOB-ENGINE-API. Semi-trusted: EL could return malformed blobs.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for cell field element range validation (< BLS_MODULUS)

reachability.notes: Attacker sends cell data with field elements >= BLS_MODULUS to cause undefined field arithmetic behavior.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct a cell where one 32-byte field element equals BLS_MODULUS (boundary value). 2. Send via P2P column sample. 3. Verify the node rejects the cell at bytes_to_bls_field conversion. 4. Test with BLS_MODULUS + 1, 2^256 - 1 (all 0xFF bytes). 5. Test: construct a cell where the element equals BLS_MODULUS - 1 (maximum valid). Verify acceptance.
executable_checks: Test: cell with field element == BLS_MODULUS, assert rejection
Test: cell with field element == BLS_MODULUS - 1, assert acceptance
Test: cell with field element == 2^256-1, assert rejection
Cross-client: verify identical rejection behavior
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W7-PCS-VERIFY-PRECOND-005. Related ambiguity: AMB-PCS-FULU-01. Critical for KZG proof security.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-UNTRUSTED-INPUT: byte length validation for PeerDAS data

reachability.notes: Primary trust boundary for PeerDAS. Any malicious peer can send arbitrary bytes.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Send raw bytes that are too short for a commitment (< BYTES_PER_COMMITMENT). Verify rejection. 2. Send bytes too long for a commitment. Verify rejection. 3. Repeat for proofs (BYTES_PER_PROOF) and cells (BYTES_PER_CELL). 4. Send completely empty payload. Verify rejection. 5. Verify the length check occurs BEFORE any deserialization attempt (no partial parsing).
executable_checks: P2P test: commitment with BYTES_PER_COMMITMENT - 1 bytes, assert rejection
P2P test: proof with BYTES_PER_PROOF + 1 bytes, assert rejection
P2P test: cell with wrong length, assert rejection
Verify: length check is first validation step (before deserialization)
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W7-PCS-SECBND-PRECOND-001. Boundary edge: EDGE-UNTRUSTED-INPUT. First line of defense for PeerDAS.

checklist.title: Falsify Pectra fork activation epoch comparison

reachability.notes: Off-by-one in epoch comparison could cause premature or delayed fork activation.

checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify Pectra activation does NOT occur at epoch 364031 (PECTRA_ACTIVATION_EPOCH - 1). 2. Verify Pectra activation DOES occur at epoch 364032 (PECTRA_ACTIVATION_EPOCH). 3. Verify activation persists at epoch 364033. 4. Cross-client: verify all clients use >= comparison with the same constant 364032 for mainnet.
executable_checks: Test: epoch 364031, assert Electra rules
Test: epoch 364032, assert Pectra rules
Cross-client: verify PECTRA_ACTIVATION_EPOCH == 364032 in all clients
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W7-EIP7600-FORK-PRECOND-001. Pre-condition: current_epoch >= 364032 for mainnet Pectra activation.
